label: Person
name: Katakalon Kekaumenos
summary:
Katakalon Kekaumenos was a prominent Byzantine general of the mid-11th century.

Born around 1010 in Thessalonica, Byzantine Empire, to a family of Greek origin, Katakalon Kekaumenos rose through the ranks of the Byzantine military during the reign of Emperor Basil II.

In 1048, he participated in the disastrous invasion of Bulgaria, which ended with the defeat of his forces at the Battle of Kleidion.

Despite this failure, Kekaumenos continued to serve under various emperors and played a key role in several military campaigns against the Seljuk Turks and the Pechenegs.

His most notable achievement came during the reign of Emperor Constantine IX Monomachus, where he successfully led an army to conquer the city of Aleppo, Syria, in 1069.

Kekaumenos died around 1081, possibly due to disease or injury sustained in battle, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most accomplished Byzantine generals of his time.

'By the sweat of our brows, we have conquered lands and achieved great victories.' - Katakalon Kekaumenos, cited in The Historia of John Skylitzes
